run.data-root: /tmp/ai-raccoon-checklist-IEBp (a VACUUM INTO copy of ~/.ai-raccoon/memory.db, 21440 entries; the live bank was never opened read-write and never written)
run.note: Focus: things changed in the last 3 releases (1.25.0 search phase attribution + VERSION-only marker, 1.26.0 repair reaches the server + repair drains what it re-ingested, 1.27.0 noise entries / watch registered leave the CLI write path). The installed global tool was already 1.27.0+d769882a (= HEAD), reused as-is; no force-update run against the user's live server on 7721. Server under test bound an ephemeral port (53262), never 7721.

derived.note: python3 .ai-badger/skills/ai-raccoon-manual-checklist/scripts/derive-facts.py . ; installed tool's `ai-raccoon --version` = 1.27.0+d769882a0b65329f0a547ad3fa6e513775897888, matching git rev-parse HEAD exactly. The script had to be fixed first — it still read <PackageVersion> from the csproj, which 1.25.0 removed (VERSION at the repo root is now the only marker, read via Directory.Build.props).

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: any checklist run after ai-raccoon 1.25.0 that used the shipped derive-facts.py
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: the script derives the version from the tree
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: derive-facts.py read <PackageVersion> from src/AiRaccoon/AiRaccoon.csproj. 1.25.0 moved the version out of the csproj into a VERSION file at the repo root (read by Directory.Build.props), so the shipped script failed loudly with 'no literal <PackageVersion> in .../AiRaccoon.csproj' on the very tree it ships for. That is the script behaving as designed — but it blocked the run and would have pressured a human to type the version by hand, the exact rot the script exists to prevent.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: Running the installed copy against this tree printed: 'derive-facts: no literal <PackageVersion> in src/AiRaccoon/AiRaccoon.csproj' and exited 1. The fix (read the csproj element first, fall back to the root VERSION file) was already merged upstream in ai-badger PR #408 but not synced to the two installed copies (~/.hermes/skills/AiRaccoon/... and .ai-badger/skills/ai-raccoon-manual-checklist/...). After syncing the merged script, it derives version=1.27.0, mcp-tool-count=27, mcp-prompt-count=2, exit 0.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: A stale script in an installed copy is the one a future run executes. This run synced both installed copies to the merged fix. Worth a den-refresh pass so other skill copies in the tree don't still carry the csproj reader.

items.expected-result: The running binary reports derived.version (1.27.0) and its embedded commit equals the tree HEAD
items.observed-result: Installed binary reports 1.27.0 and its embedded commit equals this worktree's HEAD exactly, so the install is provably this tree, not a stale build.
items.acceptance-reason: Deliberate deviation recorded: the global tool was already installed at the matching commit (a live server + MCP clients are using it), so it was reused as-is rather than force-updated — which would also have cycled the user's live server on 7721. Still the real installed binary, which is what the step exists to exercise.

items.expected-result: serve --port 0 binds an ephemeral port and reports it; 7721 is never touched
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <copy> serve --port 0 (backgrounded); read the bound URL from the server's own output
items.evidence: serve.log: 'Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:53262' and 'http://127.0.0.1:53262/mcp'; /observability reports serverInfo version 1.27.0.0. The user's own server (PID 15528) stayed on 7721.
items.observed-result: Server bound ephemeral port 53262 and reported it; the default port 7721 was never bound or restarted.
items.acceptance-reason: Default port never bound, per the skill's Never list. --restart on 7721 was deliberately not exercised because it would cycle the user's live server; the ephemeral-port bind is the part this step protects.

items.expected-result: `repair chunk-index` reports server-side scan results without the CLI opening the bank (1.26.0, ADR-0075)
items.evidence: 'chunk-index repair: 1493 source group(s) examined, 0 row(s) would reposition (dry run; pass --apply to queue it), 19 row(s) set to the unknown position (-1)'
items.observed-result: The dry-run report came back over the server (port 53262), not a CLI-held bank connection — the copy had already had chunk-index repair applied on the live bank, so 0 rows would reposition now. The 19 rows at -1 are the honest 'position unknown' marker, not a guess.
items.acceptance-reason: The verb routes through the server and reports rather than writes; --apply was deliberately not run for chunk-index because the live bank had already been repaired and 0 rows would reposition.

items.expected-result: `repair reingest --apply` queues the work to the server, and the server applies it AND drains the resulting embeddings on its next poll — nothing left pending (1.26.0 headline)
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <copy> --port 53262 repair reingest (dry run), then repair reingest --apply; wait ~20s for the 15s maintenance poll; inspect serve.log and the entries embed_state
items.evidence: dry run: '1 file(s) would reingest ... 16 row(s) affected, 16 chunk(s) to embed'. --apply: 'request committed; the server applies it and drains the resulting embeddings on its next maintenance poll (~15s) — nothing left to run by hand.' serve.log then logged: '[525] maintenance job 'apply a CLI-requested reingest repair' (repair-reingest) ran in 6638 ms' followed by '[525] maintenance job 'embed rows left pending by a write, a watch digest or a repair' (pending-embed) ran in 181 ms'. After: entries=21442, embedded=21442, zero pending.
items.observed-result: The exact 1.26.0 behaviour: the CLI never writes the bank; the server applies the reingest and the pending-embed job drains what it re-ingested, all on the 15s poll. Every one of the 21442 entries is embedded afterwards — nothing left unsearchable.
items.acceptance-reason: Both halves of the 1.26.0 claim verified on real content: server-routed apply, and the repair finishes what it re-ingested (pending-embed drain to zero).

items.expected-result: `noise entries` and `watch registered` return over the server, and the CLI's own DI graph holds no live bank connection (1.27.0, completes ADR-0075)
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <copy> --port 53262 noise entries; ... watch registered ai-badger; read the reflection gate test
items.evidence: noise entries -> 'total: 0' before the noise-write test, then 'total: 2 / HermesBackgroundProcessLog: 2' after two rejected writes. watch registered ai-badger -> 'project: ai-badger path: /Users/arasz/RiderProjects/ai-badger/docs registered: 2026-08-07... lastChange: 2026-08-17...'. CliCommandsDoNotOpenTheBankTests derives every leaf command from ConfigCommands' constructor and walks the constructed graph for a live ISqliteConnectionFactory; only EncryptionCommands/DoctorCommands/ServeCommands are allowlisted.
items.observed-result: Both read-side commands return their summaries over the HTTP control plane (the same 53262 port), and the reflection gate (the 1.27.0 test that fails on a bank-capable CLI command) names only the three sanctioned exceptions.
items.acceptance-reason: The two commands 1.27.0 closed — noise entries and watch registered — demonstrably return over the server, and the gate that makes reopening them a build failure is present (tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Unit/Setup/CliCommandsDoNotOpenTheBankTests.cs).

items.expected-result: VERSION at the repo root is the single hand-written version marker; the csproj reads it via Directory.Build.props (1.25.0)
items.command: cat VERSION; grep -n 'Version' Directory.Build.props; run derive-facts.py after the fix
items.evidence: VERSION -> '1.27.0'. Directory.Build.props:3 -> '<Version>$([System.IO.File]::ReadAllText('$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)VERSION').Trim())</Version>', plus a ValidateVersionFile target that errors on any non-bare-semver. derive-facts.py (post-fix) -> version=1.27.0, exit 0.
items.observed-result: The csproj carries no literal <PackageVersion> any more; VERSION is the only marker, validated to bare semver by the build, and the (fixed) derive-facts script reads it.
items.acceptance-reason: Verified against the source (Directory.Build.props and VERSION), not memory. This is also why derive-facts.py needed fixing this run.

items.expected-result: With fusion.noRegression.enabled.global=true (as on this machine), searches record search.fusion.* telemetry; the flag default is still false (ADR-0078)
items.command: sqlite3 read of the settings row; memory_search twice; count search.fusion.* metrics before and after
items.evidence: settings row: fusion.noRegression.enabled.global=true (inherited from the live bank; the code default is DefaultNoRegressionEnabled=false). metrics: search.fusion.top1_changed went 7 -> 9, top1_rank_delta 7 -> 9, top5_moved 7 -> 9 across the run — two enabled-flag searches wrote a fusion-diff row each.
items.observed-result: Fusion is armed on this machine (the flag is on, overriding the code default), and the enabled path writes the three fusion-diff telemetry rows per search — the evidence surface ADR-0078 ships the flag for.
items.acceptance-reason: Confirmed on the data, not the setting name alone: the telemetry row count moved exactly with the searches run under the enabled flag. The code default remains false (src/AiRaccoon.Core/Memory/Fusion/FusionConfigKeys.cs:11), so 'enabled on this machine' is a persisted setting, not a default change.

items.expected-result: memory_write returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
items.command: memory_write (positive), then two HermesProcessNoisePolicy shapes plus a clean control
items.evidence: positive -> hash e32b8c31..., stored=true. '[IMPORTANT: Background process ...' -> stored=false, reason "rejected by noise policy 'HermesBackgroundProcessLog'", hash ''. 'received signal 15' -> stored=false, same reason. clean control -> stored=true, hash bcedae17...
items.observed-result: Stored entries return real hashes; the two registered machine-notification shapes are rejected with a named reason and an empty hash, and the negative control was kept — the filter rejects what it claims, not everything.
items.acceptance-reason: One write-path policy is registered (HermesProcessNoisePolicy, ADR-0039) and its three shapes were exercised against the source (the policy class), with a clean negative control proving the filter is not reject-all.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25+vector ranking; memory_get returns its content by hash
items.command: memory_search query with no lexical overlap; memory_get by the returned hash
items.evidence: search 'an antique navigation instrument reflecting evening light in a stargazing room' -> rank 1 = the written hash e32b8c31... (stored text: 'astrolabe ... lamplight ... observatory', zero shared terms). memory_get hash e32b8c31... -> the full stored value.
items.observed-result: The query shares no literal term with the stored text, so a dead vector leg would have failed it; it ranked 1. memory_get returned the content by hash.
items.acceptance-reason: Written as a query keyword match cannot carry, per the skill's guidance; both the hybrid search and the by-hash get worked.

After: 718 rows (+57); search.fusion.* = 9 each (+2, the two enabled-flag searches); memory_performance(ai-badger) now lists memory_search count=1 with all nine search phases at real p50s (search.fts 2272.7ms / search.vector 33.3ms / search.total 2758.0ms).
